main_answer_reason: The report accurately reconstructs the opposing trial and High Court findings, the cohabitation presumption, disputed marriage proof, the stranger-provided-property limitation on asserted Rajput custom, and the High Court's daughter-priority conclusion as historical findings. It materially misidentifies counsel as claimant, reverses a school-record kinship relation, and overstates the reach of the section 50 and defense-narrative discussion. It also omits competing funding and testamentary theories and leaves several unresolved appellate issues implicit. It does not assert the withheld ultimate disposition.
uncertainties: The target appellate court's reasoning and disposition are withheld; no ultimate determination of marriage or succession priority is made here.
The complete evidentiary weight and admissibility of letters, school records and all relationship witnesses under section 50 cannot be resolved from the given extracts alone.
The record shows Raj Kumari's elopement-and-residence account and supporting testimony but does not expressly establish High Court adoption of each historical detail.
The exact rights flowing from the conflicting money-source, outsider-gift, self-acquired-property and will allegations cannot be independently adjudicated using the supplied snippets.
Some source passages contain OCR or extraction artifacts; their specific factual claims have been retained as attributed rather than silently repaired.
